A leather-and-steel war-saddle strapped behind the neck-ridge, buckles glinting in the firelight as the rider settles in.
Reins of braided chain clipped to the dragon's curved horns, taut and humming as the beast banks hard left.
War-barding plates armor the dragon's chest and shoulders, a tattered house-banner streaming wildly from the saddle-horn behind.
A riding-harness of thick oiled leather crosses the dragon's shoulders, cinched at the sternum with a heavy iron buckle.
Saddlebags of waxed canvas hang behind the saddle, stuffed with rations, rope, and sealed orders for the distant garrison.
A strapped banner pole rises from the saddle's left flank, the rider's blazon cracking and snapping in the headwind.
Foot-stirrups of forged iron loop along the scales just below the shoulder joint, letting the rider brace during dives.
A chain bridle wraps the dragon's lower jaw, linked to the horn-reins the rider controls with both gauntleted hands.
A fur-lined saddle sits low between the shoulder blades, designed for the killing cold at high-altitude mountain passes.
A quiver of black-fletched bolts is mounted left of the saddle-horn, the rider's crossbow strapped flat across the right.
A lance-rest of welded iron brackets forward of the saddle-knee, the long war-lance nestled and ready for the charge.
Trailing pennants of crimson silk are laced through the harness rings, snapping like whips as the dragon climbs steeply.
Horn-tip guards of hammered brass cap each forward horn, blunting the edges so the reins don't fray mid-flight.
Reinforced leather grips stud the spine-ridge behind the saddle, letting the rider clutch tight through violent aerial maneuvers.
A tool-roll of canvas straps just behind the cantle, holding a short-axe, a hoof-pick, and a whetstone for stops.
An emergency tether of iron cable clips the rider's belt to the saddle-ring, preventing falls during high-speed barrel rolls.
Signal flags in a tight cylinder case mount beside the quiver, the rider pulling and waving them over distant infantry.
Scale-guard panels of boiled leather pad the dragon's flanks beneath the stirrup straps, preventing chafing on the long patrols.
A map-case of oiled steel is bolted behind the rider's left knee, securing charts against the tearing high-altitude wind.
A water-skin harness straps across the dragon's lower neck, the long drinking tube routed back to the rider's saddle-hook.
Rope coils hang in loops from both saddle-sides, ready for quick deployment when landing on battlements or scaling cliff faces.
A small forge-steel lantern clips to the forward saddle-horn, shielded by a hinged brass cowl against the rushing wind.
Arming-hooks along the saddle skirt hold the rider's shield flat against the dragon's side during long overland transit flights.
A padded neck-roll bolsters the front of the saddle, bracing the rider's thighs during the gut-punching climb to altitude.
Buckled chest-straps of doubled leather cross the dragon's back ahead of the wings, anchoring the whole saddle-system in place.
